\newcommand{\resultstext}{Across all 707 training frames (1,154 annotator records, 8,199 annotated filaments), the full 5-fold teacher--student pipeline (\texttt{m1280,m1280s}+\texttt{e4}) achieves $\mathrm{PQ}=0.464$ (95\% date-bootstrap CI 0.454--0.472), $\mathrm{SQ}=0.692$ and $\mathrm{RQ}=0.670$ (5,288 true positives, 2,301 false positives and 2,911 false negatives, emitting 6.58 instances per frame on validation and 6.70 on the 180 test frames). Fold-wise PQ is consistent across the five date-grouped splits (0.464, 0.469, 0.449, 0.466 and 0.471; Fig.~\ref{fig:eval}, middle). Among overlapping prediction--annotation pairs, the mean IoU is 0.611 and the mean Dice is 0.739, compared with 0.517 and 0.660 between human annotators on the 296 multi-record frames (Fig.~\ref{fig:eval}, left). Out of 8,199 ground-truth filaments, 78.0\% (6,392) overlap exactly one prediction (one-to-one), 20.0\% (1,641) are missed, and only 2.0\% (166) touch two or more predictions; conversely, 83.4\% (6,328) of predictions overlap a single annotation, 13.9\% (1,058) are unannotated false alarms, and 2.7\% (202) bridge two or more annotations (Fig.~\ref{fig:eval}, right).}
\newcommand{\examplescaption}{The pipeline captures thin filaments and narrow barbs across GONG sites (e.g.\ 2015-04-21~Bh, 2012-05-19~Th, 2015-07-06~Th, 2011-08-03~Mh); typical disagreements occur on faint active-region fibrils or fragmented remnants where annotators also differ (2015-01-13~Ch, 2014-11-12~Bh).}
\newcommand{\discussiontext}{\emph{Strengths.} Decoupling detection at 1280~px from segmentation on $512\times512$ native-resolution crops preserves 2--5~px filament barbs ($\mathrm{SQ}=0.692$ vs.\ $0.633$ between humans) while keeping one-to-many fragmentation at 2.0\%. Self-training on 3,000 unlabeled GONG frames improves recall ($+76$ true positives for \texttt{m1280s}), and fusing teacher and student boxes via Weighted Boxes Fusion raises recognition quality ($\mathrm{RQ}: 0.663\to0.670$, PQ $0.458\to0.464$). Training the detector on every annotator record turns box confidence into a calibrated estimate of annotator consensus ($+0.015$ PQ over an untuned confidence floor $c{=}0.10$), while flip TTA adds $+0.005$ PQ. \emph{Weaknesses and future work.} Because the segmenter is restricted to a padded detector box, long curved filaments whose box is truncated by the detector cannot grow outside the crop; naive inference-time crop padding ($p{=}0.35$) lowers PQ to $0.444$ due to scale mismatch with training ($p{=}0.20$). Training the crop segmenter with multi-scale padding or adding a graph-stitching head for broken filament chains is the most direct path to further gains.}
